# Host on GitHub Pages

**Decision.** Publish [[privacy-policy-template]] as a static site on GitHub Pages, served from
`index.html` at the repository root — and **name that provider inside the legal text**, not only in
the README.

**Date.** The HTML rendering and the Pages instructions were committed together on 2026-07-10.
Confirmed live at interview, 2026-07-28: "A template, and Pages is live."

## Why

Zero build, zero cost, zero new account — the repo is already on GitHub, so publishing is a settings
toggle rather than a pipeline:

> "1. Push this repo to GitHub (done)."
> — privacy-policy/README.md, 2026-07-10

The deliverable was shaped for it: one file, no assets, no JS —
[[self-contained-single-file-html]]. Static hosting is not a compromise here, it is the exact fit.

## The unusual part: the host is in the policy

Most policies name their host, if at all, in a generic "we use service providers" clause. This one
puts GitHub in the operative text:

> "This Service is hosted on **GitHub Pages** (GitHub, Inc.). As the host, GitHub acts as a"
> — privacy-policy/PRIVACY_POLICY.md, 2026-07-10

That single sentence carries four downstream sections. §7 designates GitHub the sole processor and
links its privacy statement and Pages data-collection notice — [[controller-vs-processor]]. §4's
technical-data row exists *only* because a host keeps server logs. §10's international-transfer
clause and its Standard Contractual Clauses safeguard exist because that host's infrastructure spans
jurisdictions. §12 outsources security to the provider's HTTPS and platform hardening.

It also enables the no-tracking posture: a static host runs no analytics by default, so §6's "does
not set its own cookies" is a statement about the deployment, not just an intention.

## Alternatives rejected

| Option | Why not, as far as the repo shows |
|---|---|
| **Netlify / Vercel / Cloudflare Pages** | never mentioned anywhere in the repo |
| **Own domain + CNAME** | no `CNAME` file exists; the default `github.io` path is used |
| **A CI-built Pages deployment** | no workflow; "Deploy from a branch → `main` / root" is the documented route |
| **Markdown only, no web rendering** | the HTML rendering is the reason there is a URL to link at all |

## The cost, and the evidence gap

**Cost.** Naming one provider in the legal text couples the document to it. The README's reuse
checklist has to flag §7 as an edit point precisely because of this — see
[[one-reusable-policy-not-per-project]]. A template that hard-codes its host is slightly less
reusable and considerably more honest, and the repo takes that trade knowingly.

**Gap.** There is **no `CNAME`, no Pages workflow and no deployment artefact** anywhere in the tree.
The README's "(done)" annotates the push, not the Pages toggle. The live-URL claim therefore rests
on the interview alone — recorded as `confidence: high` because the user confirmed it, with the
explicit note that the repository corroborates nothing. **TODO:** no repo among the 15 sources
contains a footer link to the policy URL, although the README instructs exactly that.
